question: When a candidate intervention predicts different biological outcomes across worlds, does observation-process uncertainty still permit exact discrimination?
robust_discrimination_rule: An evidence channel robustly separates two worlds only when their sets of possible observed outcomes are disjoint across the full admissible observation-process universe.

bam_intervention_fixture.deterministic_parent_result: P and H each split 8 pairs; together they separate all 64 worlds.

observation_regimes.expectation: binary true outcomes map to disjoint observed outcome sets
true-positive intervention outcome admits all-zero history under p=0.75, overlapping true-negative outcome
true-negative intervention outcome can produce positive detections under q>0, overlapping true-positive outcome

hypotheses.claim: Under p=1,q=0, robust evidence design exactly reproduces the deterministic v2.5 BAM planner.
hypotheses.rule: Any mismatch in pair split counts or minimum design refutes R1.

hypotheses.claim: For every finite survey count in the protocol, admitting any p<1 causes binary presence/absence outcome supports to overlap, so neither P nor H challenge robustly separates its deterministic alias pairs.
hypotheses.rule: Any robust split under the imperfect-detection regime refutes R2.

hypotheses.claim: For every finite survey count in the protocol, admitting q>0 causes positive/negative outcome supports to overlap, so neither P nor H challenge robustly separates its deterministic alias pairs.
hypotheses.rule: Any robust split under the false-positive regime refutes R3.

hypotheses.claim: Expanding the admissible observation-process universe cannot increase robust split counts or reduce the exact minimum separating-set size.
hypotheses.rule: Any broader observation universe with stronger exact discrimination refutes R4.

hypotheses.claim: When every useful intervention has overlapping observed-outcome supports for at least one unresolved pair, the robust planner returns insufficient_library rather than using the latent biological outcome as if observed.
hypotheses.rule: Returning a separating set in such a regime refutes R5.

boundaries: The planner separates worlds on observable outcomes, not latent biological outcomes.
No probability threshold turns overlapping support into exact separation.
Larger n may change likelihood weights but cannot remove support overlap at finite n when p<1 or q>0.
This is an exact/falsification planner; probabilistic expected-information design is a separate future product.
